title: Failed create/edit/delete is invisible: the error banner sits under the scrim
body:
## Summary
Both shelf dialogs keep themselves open when a write fails (by design), but the only failure message is ProjectsView's rose banner, which renders in <main> underneath the Modal's full-screen bg-[var(--gt-ink)]/80 + backdrop-blur scrim. To a sighted user the dialog's button just returns to idle. ConfirmDelete also has no in-flight latch, so a slow delete can be pressed twice.

## Description
ProjectsView.submit returns without closing on a null answer (app/projects/ProjectsView.tsx:170-176) and the delete handler keeps the dialog open on a null `took` (:364-368). Both rely on 'the error banner above' (:207-211) to explain. But Modal portals a fixed inset-0 z-50 layer with an 80%-ink blurred backdrop (components/ui/Modal.tsx:262-275), so the banner and the nav bell are both under it. ProjectDialog's button goes 'Saving…' then back to 'Create & open' (app/_projects/ProjectDialog.tsx:195); ConfirmDelete's Delete just stays 'Delete' (:425-432). The bell does announce storage trouble for screen readers, which makes the gap sighted-only, the same shape as the Ghost defect CLAUDE.md records. Second half, same pair: ProjectDialog has a busy latch and the probe dialog-closes-on-success says 'The fix for one defect must not be the other'. ConfirmDelete's Delete has `disabled={!holds}` and no busy flag, and its onConfirm awaits remove (ProjectsView.tsx:364-367), so the double-press window the probe closed for create is still open for delete.

## Flow
- Open quick-create, fill it in, press Create & open while IndexedDB rejects (quota or blocked tab)
- The button shows Saving… then Create & open again. Nothing in the dialog changes, and the rose banner is behind the scrim
- Same for Delete: press it, nothing visibly happens. Press again and remove() runs a second time

## Expected impact
Sighted users see why a write failed in the dialog they are looking at, and delete gets the same double-submit guard as create.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the failure message for a dialog write is visible inside the dialog
Before: dialogs rendering the write error inside themselves: 0/2 (ProjectDialog, ConfirmDelete). Dialogs with an in-flight latch: 1/2
After: 2/2 and 2/2
Method: probe - source read of ProjectDialog.tsx footer (:185-199, :420-434) and ProjectsView.tsx (:165-178, :334-369)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/projects/ProjectsView.tsx:170-176,207-211,364-368; components/ui/Modal.tsx:262-275 (fixed inset-0 z-50, bg-[var(--gt-ink)]/80 backdrop-blur-sm); app/_projects/ProjectDialog.tsx:186-198,425-432 (no busy on Delete); tests/golden-path/dialog-closes-on-success.probe.spec.ts:80-93 guards busy for ProjectDialog only
verify: Extend tests/golden-path/dialog-closes-on-success.probe.spec.ts with two new tests (stripComments source reads). (1) ProjectDialog and ConfirmDelete each accept an `error` prop and render it inside their `footer`. ProjectsView passes it only after a failed write from that dialog, e.g. a `writeFailed` flag set when submit/remove resolves null and cleared on open, so a stale read error does not leak into a fresh dialog. (2) ConfirmDelete tracks busy (setBusy) and its Delete is disabled on `!holds || busy`. Both red on HEAD, green after. The error text is the machine's own message, which the real-errors exemption covers; add no explanatory prose. Then run npm run check:narration.

title: Delete confirm says 'No saved steps.' when it could not count them
body:
## Summary
ConfirmDelete waits for projectContents() so it can say what the cascade will destroy. projectContents swallows every failure into EMPTY_CONTENTS, so an unreadable count renders exactly like a project with no work: 'No saved steps.', all five cells hollow, Delete enabled. The cascade delete that follows then removes everything.

## Description
lib/projects.ts:750-762 has `catch { return EMPTY_CONTENTS; }`. ConfirmDelete treats any non-null `holds` as an answer (app/_projects/ProjectDialog.tsx:393-403), enables Delete (:427-431) and prints 'No saved steps.' (:491-492). The dialog's own comments state the rule this breaks: 'under-naming what goes is the one thing this dialog must not do' (:405-407) and 'a confirmation that has not finished saying what it will destroy has not finished being a confirmation' (:378-380). Zero-rows and failure render identically, on the app's one destructive confirm.

## Flow
- Open Delete on a project with saved frames while the steps store cannot be read (blocked tab, missing store, quota)
- The dialog reads 'No saved steps.' with five hollow cells and an enabled Delete
- Confirm: deleteProject cascades and removes the frames, including paid plates, that the dialog said did not exist

## Expected impact
The destructive confirm never understates what it will delete. An unknown count is shown as unknown (the machine's message plus hollow-dashed cells), not as zero.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the delete confirm distinguishes 'no saved steps' from 'could not count'
Before: render branches for {zero steps, count failed}: 1 (both 'No saved steps.')
After: 2 distinct branches. The failure branch shows the error and does not claim zero
Method: probe - source read lib/projects.ts:757-758 and ProjectDialog.tsx:486-493
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/projects.ts:757-758 `catch { return EMPTY_CONTENTS; }`; app/_projects/ProjectDialog.tsx:397-399 (any resolution = answer), 405-407 (the rule), 491-492 ('No saved steps.')
verify: New probe test (Node, no DOM): projectContents must not return EMPTY_CONTENTS from its catch. Make it reject, or return a {failed:true,message} variant, and assert by source read with stripComments that the catch no longer returns EMPTY_CONTENTS. A second source assertion: ConfirmDelete has a distinct failure branch that does not render 'No saved steps.'. Red on HEAD. Routed B because the root cause is in lib/projects.ts, outside this context. Grep other projectContents consumers first (git grep -n projectContents).

title: A shelf that could not be read renders 'No projects yet.' and a create CTA
body:
## Summary
When listProjects fails, useProjects sets projects to [] and raises error. ProjectsView then draws the rose banner and the EmptyShelf below it: 'No projects yet.', a hollow lane, and the screen's only filled button, New project. So failure and zero rows share one render, and the empty one asserts a falsehood: the user's projects may all be on disk.

## Description
lib/useProjects.ts:123-126 has `catch { setProjects([]); failed(...) }`, so `loading` (projects===null) is false. ProjectsView.tsx:214-222 skips the Ghost and mounts Shelf, which routes [] to EmptyShelf (:376-378). EmptyShelf prints 'No projects yet.' (app/_projects/parts.tsx:322) and its own comment calls that line a fact about 'the shelf's contents' (:312-313). On a read failure that fact is false. The filled CTA then invites a create into the same storage that just failed. There is no retry, though useProjects already exposes `reload` (lib/useProjects.ts:199).

## Flow
- IndexedDB rejects on open (another tab holds an upgrade, storage disabled)
- /projects shows the error sentence, then 'No projects yet.' and a bright New project pill
- The user believes their shelf was wiped

## Expected impact
A read failure stops claiming the shelf is empty. It shows the machine's message and a Try again bound to reload().

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an unreadable shelf is not drawn as an empty shelf
Before: render branches for {0 projects, read failed}: 1 (EmptyShelf, plus a banner in the failure case)
After: 2 branches. The read failure renders no 'No projects yet.' and offers reload
Method: probe - source read lib/useProjects.ts:123-126, ProjectsView.tsx:207-222, parts.tsx:322
Result: better
Gate: none
verify: useProjects must tell a READ failure from a write failure. ProjectsView cannot: a failed create on an empty shelf also leaves projects=[] with error set. Add `readFailed` (or keep projects null plus an error kind) to the hook's return. Probe (source read, stripComments): ProjectsView renders EmptyShelf only when the read did not fail, and the failure branch calls reload. Red on HEAD. Routed B because the distinction lives in lib/useProjects.ts.

title: Race sheet table: swimlane toggle loses button role; rowcount and rowindex lie
body:
## Summary
The group swimlane's collapse control is `<button role="rowheader" aria-expanded>`. The explicit role replaces the button role, so assistive tech announces a row header rather than an operable toggle. The table also declares aria-rowcount={rows.length}, which leaves out the header row and every swimlane row and is wrong whenever grouping is on. And because the list is windowed, the rendered rows carry no aria-rowindex, so a reader's 'row N of M' is the DOM position, not the real one.

## Description
RaceSheet.tsx:487-499: <button role="rowheader" aria-expanded=...>. Per ARIA, role overrides native semantics, so the toggle is no longer exposed as a button. Its sibling StackBar (:500-507) is a direct child of role=row without role=cell. :284: role=table aria-rowcount={rows.length}. With group=state and 300 projects that is 300, but the DOM rows are 1 header plus up to 5 swimlanes plus 300 lanes. Lane (:540-547) and Swimlane carry no aria-rowindex while useVirtual mounts a window (:329-357).

## Flow
- Group by state, then reach a swimlane with a screen reader
- Its heading is announced as a row header, the collapsed or expanded state may be read, and nothing says it can be pressed
- Scroll the window: row position announcements restart from the window's top

## Expected impact
The toggle is a real button inside a rowheader cell, the row count is true, and each windowed row reports its real index.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the group collapse control is announced as a button
Before: buttons with an overriding role=rowheader: 1. aria-rowcount equals the real row count: no (grouped). Windowed rows with aria-rowindex: 0
After: 0, yes, all
Method: probe - source read RaceSheet.tsx:284,487-507,540-547
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_projects/RaceSheet.tsx:284 (aria-rowcount={rows.length}), 487-490 (<button type="button" role="rowheader" aria-expanded>), 500-507 (StackBar not in a cell), 540-547 (no aria-rowindex). context-map.json lists app/_projects/ProjectsMatrix.tsx for project-shelf, which no longer exists; its successor app/_projects/RaceSheet.tsx (and ShelfHeader.tsx, shelf.ts, useShelf.ts, surface.ts, synthetic.ts) is unmapped. Strictly outside file_paths, so routed B; it is A-shaped if the director treats RaceSheet.tsx as the mapped matrix's successor.
verify: Add to tests/golden-path/projects-shelf.probe.spec.ts a source test over stripComments(RaceSheet.tsx). (a) No <button ...role="rowheader" (regex /<button[^>]*role="rowheader"/) and a <span role="rowheader"> wrapping the toggle. (b) aria-rowcount is computed from flat.length + 1 (header), not rows.length. (c) Lane and Swimlane receive aria-rowindex (window index + 2). Red on HEAD, green after. The render-budget probe calls Lane as a plain function, so keep its new prop optional.

title: Clicking a lane opens its parked step; Enter on it opens the next move
body:
## Summary
One race lane, two destinations. Pointer: the lane body calls onOpen(p) with no step, so the studio opens at project.phase (the bookmark). Keyboard: Enter calls open(id), which passes nextAction(p).step. The code says which one is meant: 'Enter on a lane does what its button says — the lane IS its next move', the Keycaps map advertises 'Enter: do the next move', and the lane's accessible name ends 'next: <verb>'.

## Description
RaceSheet.tsx:156-163 open = onOpen(p, nextAction(p).step), bound to Enter via useShelfKeys (:164). Lane body: onClick={() => onOpen(p)} (:546). StudioView falls back to p.phase when ?step is absent (app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:139-143). For a project parked on Research whose next move is 'Decide Script', a click lands on Research and Enter lands on Script, from the same row. The aria-label (:547) promises the Enter behaviour to screen-reader users, and mouse users get the other one.

## Flow
- Lane reads 'Decide Script' and the project is parked at Research
- Click the title area and the studio opens on Research
- Back, focus the same lane, press Enter, and the studio opens on Script

## Expected impact
One row, one meaning. The lane body does what its label and its keymap say, and the gates stay the per-step escape hatch.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - pointer and keyboard activation of one lane open the same step
Before: lanes where body-click and Enter can diverge: every lane where nextAction(p).step !== p.phase
After: 0. Body click routes through the same `open(id)` as Enter
Method: probe - source read RaceSheet.tsx:156-163,546 and StudioView.tsx:139-143
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_projects/RaceSheet.tsx:156 (comment: 'the lane IS its next move'), 157-163, 125 (KEYS 'do the next move'), 546 (onClick={() => onOpen(p)}), 547 (aria-label '..., next: ${next.verb}'); app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:139-143. context-map.json lists app/_projects/ProjectsMatrix.tsx for project-shelf, which no longer exists; its successor app/_projects/RaceSheet.tsx (and ShelfHeader.tsx, shelf.ts, useShelf.ts, surface.ts, synthetic.ts) is unmapped. Strictly outside file_paths, so routed B; it is A-shaped if the director treats RaceSheet.tsx as the mapped matrix's successor.
verify: Source test over stripComments(RaceSheet.tsx): the Lane root's onClick passes nextAction(p).step (or `next.step`) to onOpen, i.e. no bare `onOpen(p)` call. Red on HEAD (one match of /onClick=\{\(\) => onOpen\(p\)\}/), green after (0). If the operator wants the body click to resume at the bookmark, the other fix is to make Enter, the Keycaps line and the aria-label say 'open'. Either way one spelling must win.

Noted but not filed: ConfirmDelete's Delete (ProjectDialog.tsx:425-432) is a hand-rolled copy of Button variant="danger" (Primitives.tsx:75) with identical obsidian classes, so it causes no visible defect today. global-error.tsx's inline literals are deliberate (header :9-12).

lens_checked.state-coverage: useProjects load/fail/empty (lib/useProjects.ts:105-127) through ProjectsView. projectContents failure through ConfirmDelete. Wizard mint and create failure banners (CreateWizard.tsx:468-478). Ghost loading (ProjectsView.tsx:220). RaceSheet no-match vs empty shelf (distinct, OK).

Comment-only drift, not filed: ProjectDialog.tsx:61-63 says '/projects does not open this dialog when that subset is empty', which is false since quick-create is ungated (ProjectsView.tsx:239-245). stages.tsx:494-495 cites ProjectDialog saying 'Fixed at creation', which it no longer renders (now Hint 'every frame was rendered against it', ProjectDialog.tsx:261-263). Busy wording 'Saving…' and CTA 'Create & open' are consistent across dialog and wizard.
